hook: Hurricane Maria's surf, and they drove straight into it
narration: This wave broke right over a Coast Guard lifeboat, and the crew went looking for it.
Hurricane Maria was passing offshore, and the surf off Oregon Inlet was building.
Two crews from Station Oregon Inlet took their forty-seven-foot motor lifeboats out to the bar.
It was a drill, run in the same kind of seas that real rescues happen in.
The forty-seven-foot lifeboat is built to roll all the way over and come back upright.
On deck, the crew held on as the bow climbed each wave and dropped off the back.
[short pause] Then a breaker came over the rail and swept the whole deck.
outcome: The lifeboat came up through the wave, and both crews kept drilling in Maria's surf.
title: Lifeboat vs Hurricane Maria's surf
description:
On Sept. 26, 2017, two Coast Guard 47-foot Motor Lifeboat crews from Station Oregon Inlet in Nags Head, North Carolina, ran surf drills on the Oregon Inlet bar in seas stirred up by Hurricane Maria passing offshore. This is training footage.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Petty Officer 3rd Class Corinne Zilnicki and Station Oregon Inlet, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/554720/coast-guard-station-oregon-inlet-surf-drills
